_note: SYNTHETIC focus-group excerpts (placeholder until Giada's set). Speaker ids are per-session pseudonyms. Lines marked _planted contain personal information on purpose, to show the filter removes them.

excerpts.speaker: S1-A
excerpts.text: For the first time in months I made it through a full week of meetings without leaving early.

excerpts.speaker: S1-B
excerpts.text: Having someone with my dad on Tuesdays means I can actually focus at work that day.

excerpts.speaker: S1-C
excerpts.text: I didn't have to explain myself to anyone, I just signed up. That made it easier to ask.

excerpts.speaker: S1-D
excerpts.text: Booking the first visit took three phone calls, I almost gave up.

excerpts.speaker: S1-E
excerpts.text: I stopped using my sick days to cover appointments, which I was doing every month.

excerpts.speaker: S1-F
excerpts.text: What happens in March when the funding stops? I don't want to get used to this and lose it.

excerpts.speaker: S1-B
excerpts.text: The carer was great with my dad, he actually looks forward to it now.

excerpts.speaker: S1-A
excerpts.text: My manager Dave Thompson kept asking why I needed Fridays, this helped.

excerpts.speaker: S2-A
excerpts.text: I get my evenings back, so I'm less exhausted in the morning and I'm more present at work.

excerpts.speaker: S2-B
excerpts.text: Knowing it was anonymous made it easier to sign up. I didn't want HR to know my situation.

excerpts.speaker: S2-C
excerpts.text: The scheduling portal was confusing, I wasn't sure if my booking went through.

excerpts.speaker: S2-D
excerpts.text: I trust the carers now, at first I was nervous leaving my mom with a stranger.

excerpts.speaker: S2-E
excerpts.text: I've used fewer vacation days for caregiving since the pilot started.

excerpts.speaker: S2-F
excerpts.text: I'd pay part of it myself if the company didn't, it's been that useful. But I worry it ends.

excerpts.speaker: S2-C
excerpts.text: Call me at 416-555-0199 if you need someone to talk to the planners.

excerpts.speaker: S2-A
excerpts.text: I felt less guilty asking for help because it's a company program, not a favour.

excerpts.speaker: S3-A
excerpts.text: I can take a proper lunch break now instead of calling home to check in.

excerpts.speaker: S3-B
excerpts.text: Asking for help felt normal because other people on my team were doing it too.

excerpts.speaker: S3-C
excerpts.text: It took a while to figure out who to call to change a booking.

excerpts.speaker: S3-D
excerpts.text: The same carer came every week, which mattered a lot for my husband.

excerpts.speaker: S3-E
excerpts.text: My focus at work is better on the days I know he's looked after.

excerpts.speaker: S3-F
excerpts.text: I hope this continues after the pilot. If it stops I'm back to juggling everything.

excerpts.speaker: S3-B
excerpts.text: It was a relief not having to justify it to my supervisor or anyone else.

excerpts.speaker: S4-A
excerpts.text: I booked the wrong day twice because the confirmation never arrived.

excerpts.speaker: S4-B
excerpts.text: Scheduling around shift changes was hard, the booking window is too short.

excerpts.speaker: S4-C
excerpts.text: If the funding ends I don't know how we'd afford this on our own.

excerpts.speaker: S4-D
excerpts.text: Please tell us early what happens after the pilot, so we can plan.

excerpts.speaker: S4-E
excerpts.text: The carer remembered my mother's routine, that's when I started to trust it.

excerpts.speaker: S4-F
excerpts.text: I was nervous at first, but the carers were kind and on time every visit.

excerpts.speaker: S4-G
excerpts.text: I didn't have to justify anything to anyone, so asking for help felt okay.
